newsitem.title: USA: US court rules in favour of ex-Prudential manager.
newsitem.headline: US court rules in favour of ex-Prudential manager.

text.p: A branch manager fired by Prudential Insurance Co. of America should get the chance to claim in court that the company violated the state's whistleblower law, a New Jersey appellate court has ruled.
Robert L. Young sued Prudential, claiming he was fired for trying to expose and end potentially improper sales practice, such as "churning" of insurance policies.

Churning involves persuading policyholders to buy a new policiy using the cash value of an existing one, which can then drain the value of the old policy and leave policyholders unable to keep up with the payment of premiums on the new one.
It also generated a new commission for the agent.
Before accepting a promotion to manager of the Warren Hills, N.J., office, Young signed a standard National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD) agreement relegating all disputes to arbitration.
A lower court said the whistleblower claim would have to be heard in arbitration.
The appeals panel ruled that the NASD agreement included an exemption for disputes related to insurance matters.
Prudential last year agreed to settle a class-action dispute over its sales practices for at least $410 million.
A hearing on the fairness of the settlement is scheduled for next week before a federal judge in Newark.
